A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTGS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original OGBench evaluations of TTGS with HIQL, GCIQL, and QRL, including success rates, ablations, and hyperparameter sweeps.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports additional learner comparisons, manipulation results, and original diagnostic, connectivity, scaling, and replanning analyses.

M1.justification: The core graph construction, soft penalty, Dijkstra search, and adaptive execution algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix B adds an OTA-specific distance adapter that blends primitive-step and option-level estimates, while Section 4.3 introduces a separate rollout-free hop-ratio diagnostic. These are bounded extensions rather than a redesign of TTGS.

E1.justification: v2 adds manipulation evaluation on scene-play-v0, cube-triple-play-v0, puzzle-4x5-play-v0, and puzzle-4x6-play-v0 (Table 2). This extends the empirical scope beyond v1's locomotion and maze-navigation evaluations to substantially different goal-reaching tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAW and OTA, each evaluated with and without TTGS, plus an L2-kNN landmark planner (Table 7). GAS and CompDiffuser remain. GAS's pointmaze comparisons move into the fixed-setting comparison in Table 5, while its two visual-humanoid comparisons from v1 are omitted.

E3.justification: New protocols include fixed-hyperparameter TTGS/GAS comparisons, kNN and graph-size sweeps, million-triplet global/local distance sampling, and threshold-triggered replanning. The 50-rollout evaluation convention remains. The reported HIQL pointmaze-giant-stitch setting changes from (tau,T)=(12,24) in v1 Table 4 to (24,48) in v2 Table 14; the retained score does not establish that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained waypoint, no-penalty, and threshold ablations, v2 adds hard-threshold connectivity tests, L2-kNN sensitivity, triangle-inequality measurements, manipulation geometry and hop-ratio analyses, fixed-parameter transfer, graph-size scaling, and replanning tests. Table 9 also quantifies the clustering comparison that v1 described only through preliminary findings.

E5.justification: Eight-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting is retained. v2 newly states that hyperparameter screening used one random seed and that fixed seeds do not fix OGBench start/goal positions (Appendices A and L). These are additional seed disclosures, not evidence of increased evaluation replication or new significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The original HIQL/GCIQL/QRL results remain unchanged across all 15 shared benchmark rows. v2 adds scores for 12 previously untabulated maze configurations, SAW/OTA, manipulation, and supplementary analyses. GAS's main humanoidmaze-giant-stitch result changes from 8.3±4.5 to 82.4±2.5 with changed result provenance; fixed-antmaze-setting results remain separately in Table 5, so this is not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 adds the formal largest-hop-ratio definition, a hindsight-relabeling/TD derivation, and OTA option-to-step conversion and blending equations. It removes v1 Appendix C's explicit temporal-efficiency-filter formula. These are limited mathematical additions and removals; the principal value-to-distance identities remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The training-free planning claim remains, but v2 adds predicting TTGS utility without rollouts as a main contribution. Its introduction and conclusion explicitly contrast strong locomotion benefits with negligible manipulation gains and assert graceful fallback when favorable conditions fail. This materially extends the paper's contribution and applicability claims.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations involving missing intermediate states, local metric consistency, graph disconnections, and replanning oscillations, and discusses dataset-access requirements and local execution failures. It also replaces v1's caution about suboptimal subgoals with stronger safe-fallback interpretations. Appendix F's assertion of no performance risk exceeds the evidence, including degradations reported in Table 4.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: learner implementation sources, training-goal sampling distributions, OTA integration details, clustering parameters, manual tuning and selection procedures, expanded hyperparameter tables, and per-environment runtime measurements with GPU/CPU specifications. These disclosures go well beyond v1's value mappings and compact hyperparameter appendix.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands distinctions among online and offline graph planners, discussing GSP, IM-DSG, Bagatella and Martius, motion planning, and TAMP, alongside newer GCRL methods. Appendix A additionally claims TTGS is the first purely offline, test-time method in this setting. This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, related work, limitations, and conclusion are rewritten. Experiments gain dedicated manipulation and prediction subsections, while retained appendix material is reorganized within a much broader appendix structure. The narrative revision extends beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout. Figures 3 and 4 gain additional methods and an ablation, Figure 5 adds four geometry panels, and numerous experimental tables are introduced. The main comparison and hyperparameter tables gain rows and columns; v1's threshold-sweep table is retained as v2 Table 3.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses substantial validation gaps through direct connectivity and landmark-planner controls, manipulation applicability tests, and separate repository-result and fixed-setting GAS comparisons. Fuller implementation, tuning, and runtime documentation also improves reproducibility. These gains outweigh an important qualification: the new blanket safe-fallback/no-risk claims conflict with Table 4, where QRL on antmaze-medium-stitch scores 62.0% without TTGS versus 40.1% with it.
